questions.question: A hand-written reducer does `state.user.city = "Mumbai"; return state;`. Why does the UI often fail to update?
options: Reducers are not allowed to read nested fields
The returned state has the same reference, so === checks report no change
The action payload was not serialisable
questions.explanation: React-Redux and combineReducers detect changes with reference equality. Mutating and returning the same object makes them think nothing changed.

questions.question: Inside a createSlice reducer, which of these is a bug?
questions.explanation: Without braces the arrow function returns push's result (a number) while also modifying the draft. Immer throws because you both mutated and returned a value.

questions.question: Which code is allowed inside a pure reducer?
options: Computing a total from state.items and action.payload
Calling Date.now() to timestamp a new item
Saving the new state to localStorage
questions.explanation: Reducers may only compute the next state from state and action. Timestamps, storage and dispatching are side effects or non-deterministic, so they belong elsewhere.

questions.question: In a createSlice reducer, `wrongReset(state) { state = { items: [] }; }` leaves the state unchanged. What is the correct way to replace the whole slice state?
options: Set state.items = undefined and dispatch again
questions.explanation: Reassigning the state parameter only rebinds a local variable. Immer uses a returned value as the replacement state.
